summary: Commonwealth Shared Scholarships are jointly funded by the Commonwealth Scholarship Commission and UK universities for students from lower-income Commonwealth countries who could not otherwise afford to study in the UK. They fund selected one-year master's courses.
covers: A monthly stipend (£1,452, or £1,781 in London, at the most recently published rates).
Thesis and study travel grants, and child allowances for eligible single parents.
eligibility: Citizens of one of the 44 eligible Commonwealth countries.
Proof that you cannot afford to study in the UK without the scholarship.
No more than one academic year of study or work in a high-income country.
A 2:1 first degree, or a 2:2 plus a relevant postgraduate qualification. There is no age limit.
how_to_apply: Find the participating UK universities and the specific master's courses they offer under the scheme.
Apply for admission and for the scholarship directly to the university, by its own deadline.
Universities select candidates and nominate them to the CSC in March.
Results follow in the late spring or summer.
watch_out: Only selected courses are eligible, and each university sets its own deadline.
The financial-need test is central — explain clearly why you cannot study in the UK without it.
Applying to the university for admission alone is not enough; you must also complete its Shared Scholarship application.
